verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents programmatic machine management through a REST API (an OpenAPI spec with 61 paths) and the pspace CLI, explicitly including machine creation. It also has a machine 'stop state', reachable via auto-shutdown, and a community user describes hourly billing for a GPU VM. The evidence never enumerates start, stop, restart, or terminate operations for the API/CLI, and never documents that stopped machines stop accruing compute charges. missing for 10: explicit documented API/CLI start, stop, restart and delete/terminate operations, first-party documentation that billing stops for stopped or terminated machines, independent hands-on corroboration of programmatic lifecycle control.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity
the hourly rate for a standard GPU VM beats buying a local machine
